howDoI.q: How do I show a picture before a level?
How do I show a picture after a level?
How do I play a cartoon between two levels?
How do I show several pictures one after another?
How do I keep a cartoon from running too long?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Pictures and Cartoons is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has three short levels and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. Any key skips a picture. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

Nothing in this game hurts you. A picture comes up as each level begins, and a cartoon plays between the second level and the third.

pages.head: Level 1: A Picture First
pages.html:
Level 1: A Picture First

A picture came up before this level: its card, with the level's name. Three signs stand along the way. A PICTURE CAME UP BEFORE THIS LEVEL says what it was. ITS SCENE HOLDS THE INTRO PICTURE, A 320 BY 200 GIF says where it lives and how big every picture is. THE DOOR SHOWS ANOTHER AFTER THE LEVEL points ahead.

Take the nine coins, worth ten points each, and walk through the door. A second picture comes up, a painting in a gold frame with Yana cheering under it, and then the next level begins. Press any key to skip a picture, or wait a few seconds.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • The picture before. Open pics.gam in the scenes editor and pick the A Picture First scene. Its file list has two slots at the bottom: Level intro graphic and Level exit graphic. The intro slot holds frame.lst. The player shows it before the level, every time the level starts. If Yana loses a life and the level starts again, it shows again. (Nothing here can hurt them, so you will not see that.)
  • The picture itself. frame.lst is a slide list: a text file with one picture per line and how many seconds to wait. It names frame.gif, a 320 by 200 GIF drawn like any other picture.
  • The picture after. The exit slot holds post1.lst, which shows post1.gif. The player shows it when Yana leaves the scene through a link, before the next scene begins. It is not shown when they lose a life. It is shown for every link out of the scene, not only the door.
  • The signs. Each is a few ordinary blocks with words drawn into them, as in the Say Something Starter. Look at sign.frame0.sign.00 and its neighbors in pics.bbl.

pages.head: Level 2: A Cartoon Between
pages.html:
Level 2: A Cartoon Between

Three signs. A CARTOON IS AN FLI FILE THAT MOVES says what to expect. THE EXIT SLOT PLAYS IT WHEN YOU LEAVE says where it lives, and WALK THROUGH THE DOOR TO WATCH IT is the invitation.

Take the nine coins and go through the door. A seed sits on a mound, the sun comes up, a stalk grows with two leaves, a daisy opens, and Yana cheers. It plays for about three and a half seconds, and then level 3 begins.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • The cartoon. bloom.fli is an FLI file: a short animation of 320 by 200 pictures with a pause between them. This one has 40 frames and waits 6/70 of a second after each. It is drawn frame by frame in code, but an FLI from any animation program works the same.
  • Where it goes. In the scenes editor, the A Cartoon Between scene has bloom.fli in its Level exit graphic slot. A cartoon can go in either slot, or in a slide list beside pictures.
  • The palette. An FLI sets its own colors in its first frame, as a GIF does. This one uses the game's palette, so the grass in the cartoon is the grass in the levels. The cartoon fades in and out through black so the cut to the level is soft.
  • Why it ends at the door. The player plays the exit file after Yana takes the link and before the next scene loads. So a cartoon between two levels goes in the first level's exit slot (or the second level's intro slot).

pages.head: Level 3: Keep It Short
pages.html:
Level 3: Keep It Short

Two pictures came up before this level, one after the other. A LIST SHOWS TWO PICTURES, ONE AFTER ANOTHER says so. A CARTOON PLAYS TO ITS LAST FRAME and SO KEEP IT SHORT, OR CUT IT INTO CLIPS say what a cartoon can't do.

Take the nine coins and go through the door to the ending.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 3 is made

  • A list. The intro slot holds short.lst, a slide list of two pictures: short.gif for three seconds, then short2.gif for three more. A list can hold GIFs, FLIs and text pages in any mix, and a list can name another list.
  • Short cartoons. The player plays every frame of a cartoon before it looks at the keyboard, so Esc cannot stop one halfway. A long cartoon cut into several short FLI files and put in a list answers at each join. The cartoon in level 2 is under four seconds, so it is a single file.
  • The ending. The last door links to the The End scene in pics.gam, which shows won.lst.

pages.head: What Game-Maker cannot do
pages.html:
What Game-Maker cannot do

  • Sizes. The screen is 320 by 200. The player draws a picture from the top left corner and does not scale it, so draw every GIF and every FLI at exactly 320 by 200. A smaller one is not stretched to fit.
  • Colors. A picture or cartoon has at most 256 colors, which is the screen's limit. Each carries its own palette, and the level brings back its own colors afterward.
  • Sound. An FLI is silent: the format carries no sound, so a sound effect cannot ride on one of its frames. Music is a separate file for the scene.
  • Skipping a cartoon. A cartoon cannot be stopped partway. A picture can be skipped with any key.
  • Playing during a level. Pictures and cartoons come before or after a scene, never in the middle of one. Nothing in the level moves while they play.
  • Choosing by what happened. The after picture always follows a link. One link can lead to only one scene, and a scene has one exit slot. For a different cartoon, use a different link and scene.
  • Looping. A cartoon plays once. It does not repeat.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Draw a new 320 by 200 picture in any paint program, save it as a GIF named post1.gif, and put it in the game's folder. Walk through level 1's door.
  • Open frame.lst and change how many seconds the card waits.
  • In the scenes editor, move bloom.fli from level 2's exit slot to level 3's intro slot.
  • Add a third picture to short.lst.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.

box.back: A small explorer in a pink beanie crosses three short rooms of signs. A picture comes up as each room begins, another as they leave the first, and a little cartoon plays between the second and the third. Read the signs, watch, then open the game in Game-Maker and put in pictures of your own.

A picture before a level and one after it, and a cartoon between levels
Made to be copied and taken apart

blurb: Three short rooms about pictures and cartoons. A picture is a GIF file; a cartoon is an FLI file. A scene can show one before its level and another after it, and a list shows several in a row. Signs in the levels say which is which. Play it, then open it in Game-Maker and swap in pictures of your own.
